subject: Key escrow & split-control evidence for SIG assessment — Meditech
body:
From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@meditech.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@meditech.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Key escrow / split-control evidence for SIG questionnaire

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for taking the SIG packet. As part of our information security review we need a short evidence bundle covering how Redwood handles key escrow, split control, and custodial access for customer keys (BYOK and Redwood-managed keys). Specifically our security team wants: 

- Any formal key escrow or escrow-avoidance policy (if applicable)
- HSM attestation or vendor cert for the devices used for root key protection
- Proof of split-control / dual control for key import/export (procedural description + logs)
- High-level rotation schedule and last rotation timestamps for keys used to encrypt customer data at rest
- A small redacted sample of access logs showing who performed key operations (create/import/rotate) in the last 90 days

We don’t need raw PII in logs — just metadata (actor, operation, timestamp, request id). If you can include one-page summaries for each item that would be ideal. Do you have an ETA? We’re trying to close the SIG in the coming week.

Best,
Megan Liu
Senior InfoSec Analyst
Meditech

---

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@meditech.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Key escrow / split-control evidence for SIG questionnaire

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear list. We can provide all of that. Quick notes:

- Redwood does not escrow customer keys unless explicitly requested in a signed contract; BYOK customers keep control and we only hold wrapped keys when customers opt into managed-key recovery.
- Root and wrapping keys are stored in HSMs (FIPS 140-2/3 module) with vendor attestation — I will attach the latest attestation.
- Dual-control (split-control) is enforced for sensitive key operations: two-person approval for root import/export and an auditable workflow.
- We can supply a redacted access-log snippet and a concise rotation schedule.

I’ll pull the items and coordinate with Dev to get the logs and signatures redacted. Expect a package by EOD Thursday Pacific.

Quick ask: do you need the documentation to include diagrams of the split control workflow, or is a textual SOP sufficient for your SIG reviewer?

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

---

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Megan Liu <megan.liu@meditech.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Key escrow / split-control evidence for SIG questionnaire

Megan / Ava — attaching the files we discussed. Notes inline.

Attachments:
- escrow_agreement_v1.pdf (attachment) — our standard clause template for escrow/managed recovery; shows opt-in wording and customer consent fields.
- hsm-attestation-2026-10-31.pdf (attachment) — vendor attestation for our HSM fleet used for root/wrapping keys.
- key_rotation_schedule.csv (attachment) — high-level schedule (rotation frequency, last rotated, responsible owner).
- access_logs_snippet.txt (attachment) — redacted lines with actor_id, operation, timestamp, request_id; names replaced with role/team aliases per our redaction policy.

Important operational details we included in the package:
- We never perform automated unescrow of customer private keys without a documented, signed request and two approvers (security owner + engineering manager).
- Split-control uses an internal KMS workflow: crypto-ops + security approvals + HSM CSR-based import; each step creates an immutable audit record.
- The rotation schedule documents both customer-data encryption keys (DEKs) rotated on a 90-day cadence and wrapping/root keys rotated annually (with emergency rotation procedures).

If you need additional log fields (IP address, full actor email), let us know and we can discuss a secure transfer mechanism.

- Dev
Senior SRE, Crypto Ops
Redwood Inference

---

From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@meditech.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@meditech.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Key escrow / split-control evidence for SIG questionnaire

Thanks — this looks good. A couple follow-ups from our reviewer: 

1) For the access logs sample: can you include the MFA challenge_result field (success/failed) for the approving actor? They want to see that approvals are gated by MFA. Redacted is fine.
2) For the escrow_agreement_v1.pdf — can you confirm whether the opt-in flow requires a DocuSign signature from the customer AND a security team acceptance stamp? If so, can you provide an example signed document (redacted)?

If you can provide the MFA field and the signed example by Friday EOD Pacific we should be able to finish our internal review.

Best,
Megan

---

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@meditech.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Key escrow / split-control evidence for SIG questionnaire

Hi Megan — Monica here (Enterprise Security Liaison). Quick confirmation on two points: 

- DocuSign: Yes — our managed-key escrow requires a signed customer consent via DocuSign plus an internal acceptance record stamped by the security team. I have placed a redacted example in the link below (DocuSign audit + signature page only).
- MFA for approvals: We enforce MFA for all approvers. We will add the MFA challenge_result field to the redacted log extract.

Deliverables (final):
- Smaller evidence pack with the redacted DocuSign sample (signature + audit trail), updated access_logs_snippet.txt (now includes MFA result), and a one-page SOP diagram (text + small flowchart).
- A short cover note explaining that escrow is opt-in and the fallback process is customer-driven.

Link to the signable example and final bundle: https://app.docusign.com/meditech/escrow/12345

Ava / Dev — I’ll message you separately to confirm the log export and to redact the DocuSign PDF before we push it to the external link. Megan, we’ll get the updated bundle to you by end-of-day Friday.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Security Liaison
Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs included above: escrow_agreement_v1.pdf, hsm-attestation-2026-10-31.pdf, key_rotation_schedule.csv, access_logs_snippet.txt]
